summary: Sierra Leone's pledges combine restoration, conservation and agricultural action. Restoration includes a 5-million-tree initiative within 4–5 years, 14,000 ha of degraded-land reforestation (an area equal to about 0.7% of current forest cover), 5,000 ha of mangrove restoration and management over 10 years, and separate 60,000 and 120,000 ha restoration targets; by 2035, 200,000 ha of forest is earmarked for restoration, while 3,000–30,000 ha of mangroves could be rehabilitated by 2030. Conservation includes 50,000 ha under community management or co-management (≈2.4% of current forest), forest and mangrove management goals of 200,000 and 100,000 ha by 2035, and a 50% vulnerability-reduction goal. Agriculture scales unburned and sedentary-farming areas from 30,000 ha in 2030 to 60,000 and 90,000 ha in 2035, places 30,000 ha under CSA by 2030, and expands irrigation to 45,000 ha by 2035 (≈0.9% of the current agricultural area).
